experiment: E20 short aliases for UML3 keywords, and the usage form of a keyword
setup: A UML3 keyword is the short name of its metadata definition ('metadata def <classType> classType'), and SysML v2 allows one short name per element, so a shorter spelling has to be an alias. The probe declares 'alias cls for classType' and applies '#cls' to a definition and to a usage, next to the spelled-out '#classType'.

predictions.claim: The probe loads with 0 builder errors: an alias is a namespace member, so '#cls' resolves like '#classType'
The validation engine reports no ERROR for the probe package
The keyword has the same effect through the alias: AliasedClass specializes UML3Core::Class, exactly as SpelledClass does
A keyword on a usage works the same way: aliasedClassUsage subsets UML3Core::classes
tools/check_names.py accepts the alias spelling (it resolves metadata names through the index), or reports it, which would mean the checker needs to follow aliases
